summary_html: **Mandatory reporters** (designated professionals) must report suspected child abuse or neglect. Federal law sets the funding and policy floor (CAPTA) and mandates reporter frameworks on federal lands/facilities (VICAA).
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — federal floor for state reporting systems  
- **Victims of Child Abuse Act (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — includes federal-facility reporter duties (recodified from former 42 U.S.C. §13031)

primary_citations.citation_text: Iowa - Title VI, Chapter 232 (Juvenile Justice – includes mandatory reporting and child in need of assistance)

regulations_applicable.title: Agency 249 - EARLY CHILDHOOD IOWA STATE BOARD
Agency 428 - Criminal And Juvenile Justice Planning Division

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: A physician who gave the DHS child-abuse investigator his honest opinion that the father's explanation of an infant's spiral fracture was plausible was immune from civil liability under Iowa Code section 232.73, because that immunity turns on the subjective good faith of the person reporting or assisting in the assessment, not on whether he was negligent.
key_cases.relevance: Sets Iowa's controlling standard for reporter and participant immunity under Iowa Code section 232.73 — subjective good faith, not reasonableness — which is the liability rule every mandatory reporter operates under.
key_cases.quote: To avoid summary judgment, the plaintiff must have evidence the defendant acted dishonestly, not merely carelessly, in assisting the DHS.

key_cases.case_name: McCracken v. Iowa Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: DHS had statutory authority to investigate the same alleged incident a second time and to enter a founded report even though an earlier investigation had produced an unfounded report that was expunged; the second investigator lawfully accessed the expunged unfounded information under Iowa Code section 235A.15(3), and the father's constitutional due-process objections to the ALJ hearing were not preserved.
key_cases.relevance: Holds that a department social worker who learns of suspected abuse is herself a mandatory reporter bound by Iowa Code section 232.69 and exposed to civil and criminal penalties for silence, so a new disclosure restarts the reporting duty.
key_cases.quote: the department had statutory authority to conduct an investigation involving the alleged sexual abuse, even though a previous investigation of the same allegation resulted in an unfounded report

state_agency.name: Iowa Department of Health and Human Services, Child Protective Services

mandatory_reporters: Health practitioners who examine, attend, or treat a child — § 232.69(1)(a)
Employees/operators of public or private health care facilities — § 232.69(1)(b)(2)
Licensed school employees, certified para-educators, coaching-authorization holders, school employees age 18 or older, and community college instructors — § 232.69(1)(b)(4)

Employees/operators of licensed child care centers, registered child development homes, head start programs, family development and self-sufficiency grant programs, and HOPES–Healthy Families Iowa programs — § 232.69(1)(b)(5)
Employees/operators of licensed substance use disorder programs or facilities — § 232.69(1)(b)(6)
Employees of department institutions listed in Iowa Code § 218.1 — § 232.69(1)(b)(7)
Employees/operators of juvenile detention or juvenile shelter care facilities — § 232.69(1)(b)(8)
Employees/operators of child foster care facilities — § 232.69(1)(b)(9)
Employees/operators of providers of services to children funded under a federally approved medical assistance home and community-based services waiver — § 232.69(1)(b)(13)
Employees, operators, owners, and others who perform duties for certified children's residential facilities — § 232.69(1)(b)(14)
reporting_details: Iowa is a designated-professional reporting state: the classes of persons listed in Iowa Code § 232.69(1) must report suspected child abuse within 24 hours, while any other person may report but is not required to (Iowa Code § 232.69(2)).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours (child abuse assessment) or 72 hours (family assessment)
20 business days (child abuse assessment); 10 business days (family assessment)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of the child abuse report

notice_requirements.timing: Within 5 working days of commencing the assessment (Iowa Code § 232.71B(2)); a court may direct the department to withhold notification if it would endanger the child or other persons

parent_rights_at_moment: Right to refuse entry without warrant
what_to_say: I do not consent to entry without a warrant
Please provide your card and the allegations in writing
I will have my attorney contact you
what_not_to_do: Do not let them in 'just to look'
